title: Deployment safety check-ins and lifted blockers - 2027-02-11
content:
Context: quick mid-week digest from the private-deploy team. This doc is a running log of the safety-check items we reviewed, blockers that were lifted in the last 48h, and remaining risks that need a follow-up. Intended audience: field engineers, SRE oncall, and PMs for the affected customers.

Highlights:
- Two customer installs moved from 'degraded' -> 'stable' after targeted network ACL fixes and KV cache warm-up changes.
- We conducted a light smoke of the rollback path for the new kernel-optimized runtime (lab-proxy environment). No regressions observed on small seq lengths; larger seq regression ticket created.
- Re-evaluated blast-radius matrix for canary > 20% traffic on Dedicated pools. Added an extra safety gate: automatic fallback to the previous quantized variant if 5xx rate exceeds 0.6% for 3m.

Standup notes (2027-02-11, 09:30 PST):
- Riley: Customer "Catalyst Health" reported intermittent 5xx during high-concurrency ingest (p95 latency spike + cache-thrash). Root cause sketch: MTU mismatch on transit switch + iptables rule backlog on the host. Temporary mitigation applied (increase net.core.netdev_max_backlog), long term: infra ticket to harmonize MTU across the edge stack. See ENG-4523.
- Priya: Onprem deployment for BankWave finished post-install validation. Remaining item: KMS policy review for HSM integration (security team to confirm scope). Customer requested audit snapshot next week.
- Michael: Rollout of kernel-optimized runtime started for internal testbeds; saw 1.2% token output variance on long-chat tests (seq > 2048). Created ONPREM-981 for evaluation against baseline quantized model.
- Ops Oncall: Observability gap for prefix-caching TTLs — missing traces on partial cache hits. Instrumentation PR linked above.

Blocked -> lifted (last 48h):
- Blocker: Customer network egress rule that was dropping TLS re-negotiation packets -> lifted after coordinated firewall rewrite with customer netops (root cause: deep inspection appliance flagged our keepalive pattern). Follow-ups: add a fallback TLS handshake jitter and update install checklist.
- Blocker: Node provisioning script failed in 12.04 kernel images due to device-mapper version mismatch -> lifted by pinning dm-udev to 2.03. Action: add kernel matrix to release-engineering checklist.

Open risks / actions:
- Risk: MTU mismatch scaling to multiple customers could cause correlated latency spikes. Owner: Riley. Due: 2027-02-18. Action: create a network-scan job in the install agent and include MTU detection step.
- Risk: Output quality variance after kernel runtime change for long sequences. Owner: Michael + Research. Due: 2027-02-16. Action: run 2000+ sequence evals, collect token-level diffs, and create rollback thresholds.
- Action: Security to validate BankWave KMS/HSM mapping and provide signed policy artifacts. Owner: Priya. Due: 2027-02-15.
- Action: Add an explicit check to the field-runbook: verify time sync (chrony) and ntp drift < 50ms before moving to canary. Owner: Asha. Due: 2027-02-14.

Experiment notes / heuristics learned:
- Increasing net.core.netdev_max_backlog from 1000 -> 5000 reduced transient accept queue drops on small instances under synthetic load. Not a final fix, but a good emergent mitigation while we eliminate MTU/fragmentation issues at the switch.
- When a customer firewall performs TLS deep inspection, our keepalive frequency pattern can look like a malformed flow. Adding a randomized jitter to keepalive solved re-negotiation failures in 2/2 repro cases.

Customer-impact summary:
- Catalyst Health: short incidents during peak test window. SLA impact: none (no user-facing downtime), but internal SLO for 99.9 latency affected during narrow window. Next steps: deploy MTU check and push a low-risk priming traffic pattern to reduce cold cache thrash.
- BankWave: install validated; awaiting KMS confirmation before final sign-off.

Meeting asks / decisions needed from PMs/security/infra:
- PMs: approve moving BankWave to 'production' pointer once KMS is confirmed. If no reply by 2027-02-15, we'll default to a temporary hold.
- Security: expedited review for HSM policy (Priya). Provide ETA.
- Infra: agree on a host-level template that includes the netdev backlog change and explicit MTU check. This should be coordinated with customers that require strict MTU values.

Quick wins for next 72h:
- Add MTU probe to install-agent (Riley) and roll to lab-proxy for smoke.
- Expand canary gate to include cache-hit ratio delta threshold (Asha + Michael).
- Postmortem draft for the TLS re-negotiation incident (owners: Riley + Customer Success).

Notes-to-self / misc:
- Keep this doc intentionally terse; longer postmortems should live in Confluence but link back here.
- If you are triaging in the next 24h, grep the logs for 'tls-reneg' and 'netdev_backlog'—those strings helped correlate two separate incidents.

Attachments / useful links:
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2045
- field runbook (latest): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Field+Safety+Runbook
- Tickets: ENG-4523, ONPREM-981

End of note. Next safety check: Friday 2027-02-12 10:00 PST (light smoke + canary status).
summary: Mid-week private-deploy safety check: two blockers lifted (TLS re-neg and node provisioning), MTU mismatch identified as a recurring risk, kernel runtime long-seq variance requires evaluation. Action owners assigned with 1-2 week SLAs.
